description: Create the foundational documentation files: philosophy.md, architecture.md, project-structure.md, and escape-hatch.md. These establish the core principles and high-level system understanding that other docs reference.
steps: Create docs/philosophy.md covering: the 6 core non-negotiable rules, non-goals (Docker, K8s, Postgres, Redis, multi-runtime JS), graduation path (when to leave Doot), the 'remove decisions not add configuration' principle, and the core bet (99% of apps don't need distributed infra).

Create docs/architecture.md covering: system overview with component diagram (ASCII/mermaid), single binary architecture (CLI + dootd modes), data flow from .do files through compiler to native binary, runtime architecture (HTTP server, SQLite, job worker pool, session store), and how components interact.

Create docs/project-structure.md covering: canonical directory layout (app.do, feature files, views/, static/, uploads/, .env, migrations/), feature-fused vs MVC explanation, what each file/directory is for, conventions for naming, and examples.

Create docs/escape-hatch.md covering: the native block semantics, keyword choice (verbose by design), scoping rules (block-level only, never file-level), full Nim stdlib access, DSL primitives remain accessible inside native blocks, documentation placement philosophy, limitations, and when to use it vs when to just graduate from Doot.
acceptance_criteria: docs/philosophy.md exists and covers all 6 core rules with explanation
docs/architecture.md exists with component diagram and data flow
docs/project-structure.md exists with full directory layout and conventions
docs/escape-hatch.md exists with native block syntax examples and scoping rules
All files are internally consistent with each other and reference the same terminology
verification: Verify all 4 files exist: ls docs/philosophy.md docs/architecture.md docs/project-structure.md docs/escape-hatch.md
Verify files are non-empty and contain proper markdown headings
